answer: Payout sits at the zenith of a horizon that only moves one epoch at a time. Each claim drops an anchor bond whose depth equals the verified epochs of stranger-checked work behind it; the anchor can only sink one step per epoch, each step paid with a fresh job for a stranger beyond the horizon. A clone starts at the surface, so n clones need n anchors, n times depth jobs and n epochs of waiting, while one honest agent pays once. The zenith prize per funding trail is fixed and split n ways, so cloning costs n times more for 1/n of the prize.
